label: prf:three-calibration-inputs
title: Proof of three calibration inputs
html:
Proof

The three-parameter count follows directly from prop:three-parameters-wedderburn: on-shell + gauge-invariance restricts the categorical action to a 3-dimensional real parameter family. The choice of which three external measurements pin the three parameters is conventional but constrained by:

  1. Dimensional analysis. The modulus q_0 is pinned canonical by the dimensionless ratio m_\mu/m_e (the most precise proxy for CAL-2, P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}); two dimensional proxies (m_e, m_\pi) pin the leptonic mass scale and the meson scale. The hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 is derived from m_e and q_0; \mathfrak{Q}_\beta is the CAL-2 proxy and, once q_0 is pinned by m_\mu/m_e, a cross-check — neither is an independent input.

  2. Precision. m_e has CODATA precision 2.9 \times 10^{-10}; m_\mu/m_e has 2.2 \times 10^{-8} (limited by m_\mu); m_\pi has PDG precision \sim 2 \times 10^{-6}. Each is among the most precisely measured quantities in its sector. In the Physical-Observations layer q_0 may instead be anchored on the proton ratio m_p/m_e (6 \times 10^{-11}), the most precise anchor available.

  3. Naturality. The electron is the simplest charged lepton; the m_\mu/m_e ratio dimensionalises to \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), the simplest hyperbolic knot invariant; the free-neutron decay is the simplest hadronic decay (one crossing change, no nuclear environment).

The categorical mass identity prop:categorical-mass-markov gives every mass as \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))| with \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q_0); multiplication by m_e converts to MeV. For Q-values, the brane-tower correction in the hadronic sector is captured by the dimensionless factor \hat{\mathcal{O}}(q_0), with E_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n)/|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| providing the symbolic-to-numeric bridge for the hadronic energy scale.

The forbidden-substitution clauses are not mathematically necessary; they are editorial — they are the conditions under which the paper's "three-parameter" claim is honest.

\square
